images.title: Finding the median by running totals
images.purpose: Shows the 36 family sizes as one row of 36 cells in blocks, with the 18th and 19th cells landing in the block of size 5.
images.composition: One long horizontal row of 36 small square cells across the middle of the frame, grouped into four coloured blocks, with running totals under two block ends and a marker on the two middle cells. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: A single row of 36 equal square cells, touching, thin dark outlines. Cells 1 to 3 are light grey (#6B7280, pale) with the label 'size 3' above them. Cells 4 to 14 are teal (#0072B2), 11 cells, with the label 'size 4' above them. Cells 15 to 23 are amber (#E69F00), 9 cells, with the label 'size 5' above them. Cells 24 to 36 are light grey, 13 cells, with the label 'sizes 6 to 10' above them. Under the right edge of cell 14 the number '14' and under the right edge of cell 23 the number '23'. Cells 18 and 19 have a thick reddish purple (#CC79A7) outline, and a reddish purple arrow below them points up with the labels '18th and 19th' and 'median 5' stacked under it. Exactly 36 cells: 3 + 11 + 9 + 13.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Add frequencies until you pass the middle positions; both middle values are 5.
images.description: Shows the 36 family sizes as one row of 36 cells in blocks, with the 18th and 19th cells landing in the block of size 5.
images.context: Frequencies 3, 11, 9, 7, 3, 1, 1, 1 for sizes 3 to 10; running totals 3, 14, 23; 36 values.
images.teaching_notes: Cells 24 to 36 merge sizes 6 to 10 (7 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 13) to keep the picture uncluttered.

image_decisions.why: Running totals are a counting picture: seeing the 36 positions in blocks shows where the middle falls.
